title: The backward pawn
line: A pawn its neighbors cannot defend.

steps.text: Black's pawn on d6 is backward. One pawn beside it is gone and the other has moved past it, so no black pawn can guard it now.
It cannot step forward safely either: White guards the square in front of it. Tap that square.
steps.hint: Black's pawns move down the board.
steps.after: No black pawn can attack that square now.

steps.text: Black's knight on f6 guards that square. Take it with your bishop.

also.c3d5: That goes to the square at once, and it works too. This lesson first takes the knight that guards it.

steps.after: A pawn takes back, and one guard of the square is gone.

steps.text: Now put your knight on the square in front of the backward pawn.
steps.hint: It is the knight nearer the middle of the board.
steps.after: The knight blocks the pawn, and no black pawn can attack it now. To remove it, Black would have to trade a piece for it.

summary: A backward pawn cannot be guarded by a pawn or step forward safely. Put a piece on the square in front of it.
